title: Find Best Resubmission Score by Student Status
prompt: The K-12 homework app tracks student accounts in the `students` table, which includes an `account_status` field ('active' or 'suspended'). The `resubmissions` table records every time a student resubmits an assignment to improve their grade, with each row containing the student_id, assignment_id, resubmission_date, and improved_score. A student may resubmit the same assignment multiple times. Write a query that returns one row per student showing their student_id, account_status, and best_resubmission_score (the highest improved_score across all their resubmissions). However, only students with account_status = 'active' should receive their actual best score; students with account_status = 'suspended' should show NULL for best_resubmission_score. Every student in the students table must appear in the output exactly once. Order the results by student_id ascending.
schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE students (student_id INT PRIMARY KEY, student_name VARCHAR(100), account_status VARCHAR(20)); CREATE TABLE resubmissions (resubmission_id INT PRIMARY KEY, student_id INT, assignment_id INT, resubmission_date DATE, improved_score INT);
example_input_data: INSERT INTO students (student_id, student_name, account_status) VALUES (1, 'Alice Chen', 'active'), (2, 'Bob Martinez', 'active'), (3, 'Carla Wu', 'suspended'), (4, 'Dan Lee', 'active'), (5, 'Eva Kim', 'suspended'); INSERT INTO resubmissions (resubmission_id, student_id, assignment_id, resubmission_date, improved_score) VALUES (101, 1, 10, '2024-01-15', 85), (102, 1, 10, '2024-01-20', 92), (103, 1, 11, '2024-01-18', 78), (104, 2, 12, '2024-01-16', 88), (105, 3, 13, '2024-01-17', 95), (106, 3, 13, '2024-01-22', 98), (107, 4, 14, '2024-01-19', 74);

composite_moves: look up gate attribute (account_status) from students table
per-entity pick: MAX(improved_score) grouped by student_id from resubmissions table
gate with CASE: if account_status = 'active' return MAX score, else NULL

hints: You need to combine information from both tables, checking each student's account status while finding their best score across all resubmissions.
Use a LEFT JOIN from students to an aggregated version of resubmissions (grouped by student_id with MAX(improved_score)), then apply a CASE expression that checks the account_status column.

The solution is: SELECT s.student_id, s.account_status, CASE WHEN s.account_status = 'active' THEN MAX(r.improved_score) ELSE NULL END FROM students s LEFT JOIN resubmissions r ... GROUP BY s.student_id, s.account_status ORDER BY s.student_id;
answer_key: SELECT s.student_id, s.account_status, CASE WHEN s.account_status = 'active' THEN MAX(r.improved_score) ELSE NULL END AS best_resubmission_score FROM students s LEFT JOIN resubmissions r ON s.student_id = r.student_id GROUP BY s.student_id, s.account_status ORDER BY s.student_id;

_meta.scenario: a K-12 homework app tracking assignment turn-in and grade improvement
